member.name: T:DesignKit.Controls.JsonView
member.summary: Read-only, syntax-coloured JSON viewer — for showing a config file, a saved recipe or an instrument response without making the user read one unbroken grey wall of text. The six token colours are dependency properties whose defaults come from theme brushes, so they follow a runtime theme switch like everything else.
member.remarks:
Hosts a read-only rather than drawing text itself, so the content stays selectable and copyable (Ctrl+C, right-click) — the thing people actually want from a viewer like this. The tokenizer is a single forward pass tuned for pretty-printed JSON; malformed input degrades into punctuation runs instead of throwing, because a viewer that crashes on a half-written file is worse than one that renders it plainly. Adjacent same-kind tokens are merged into one and added in a single pass, which keeps large documents from spending their time in layout.
This is a viewer, not an editor: no folding, no line numbers, no editing. Look defined entirely by the default style in Themes/Generic.xaml.

member.summary: Watches the window that owns a control and reports when it is activated or deactivated.
member.remarks:
Every floating surface in this kit lives in a , and a WPF Popup is its own top-level always-on-top window. It does NOT hide when the app behind it loses activation, so alt-tabbing away leaves the flyout, tip or dialog stranded on top of whatever application the user switched to. StaysOpen="False" does not help: that is light dismiss, which reacts to a click, not to the app losing focus.
Attaching is deliberately explicit and paired with rather than done once at construction: the window outlives the control, so a handler left attached would keep the control (and everything it holds) alive for the window's lifetime. member.name: T:DesignKit.Motion
member.summary: Attached properties that put a standard transition on any element, so screens do not have to hand-write Storyboards. Named after the WinUI theme transitions they stand in for: is EntranceThemeTransition (something appearing in place), is PaneThemeTransition (a panel sliding in from an edge). Durations and curves come from the theme's motion axis (Fluent.Motion.xaml), so timing is tuned in one file - set every duration to zero there and the whole system goes still without a single call site changing.

member.name: F:DesignKit.Motion.PaneTransitionProperty
member.summary: Slides the element in from the edge it is docked against, so an opening pane or flyout reads as coming from somewhere instead of blinking into existence - the stand-in for WinUI's PaneThemeTransition. The edge is taken from the element's own alignment, so a right-docked pane comes in from the right with no extra configuration.
